relations.note: Izanagi’s killing of Kagutsuchi causes blood on his sword to generate Takemikazuchi.
Takemikazuchi or his ancestral line emerges from blood shed when Kagutsuchi is killed.
The sword-deity Ame-no-Ohabari is explicitly called Takemikazuchi’s father.
Ame-no-Ohabari recommends his son Takemikazuchi for the land-subjugation mission.
Mikahayahi and Takemikazuchi are co-generated from blood on Izanagi’s sword.
One genealogy makes Mikahayahi Takemikazuchi’s grandparent through Hihayahi.
Takemikazuchi descends from Mikahayahi through the Hihayahi lineage.
Hihayahi and Takemikazuchi are co-generated from blood on Izanagi’s sword.
A variant genealogy names Hihayahi as Takemikazuchi’s parent.
Takemikazuchi is a son or descendant within Hihayahi’s lineage.
Amaterasu commissions Takemikazuchi to secure the terrestrial realm for the heavenly lineage.
At Amaterasu’s request, Takemikazuchi sends his conquest sword instead of descending personally.
Takagi participates with Amaterasu in selecting and commissioning Takemikazuchi as heavenly envoy.
Ame-no-Torifune accompanies Takemikazuchi to demand the transfer of Ōkuninushi’s land.
Takemikazuchi protests when Futsunushi alone is selected, asserting his own martial standing.
Takemikazuchi and Futsunushi descend together as heavenly land-subjugators.
Takemikazuchi demands that Ōkuninushi surrender the terrestrial realm; he eventually yields.
Takemikazuchi’s demand is referred to Kotoshironushi, who consents to the transfer and withdraws.
Takemikazuchi transforms his arm, crushes and throws Takeminakata, then forces his submission at Suwa.

relations.myth: Suppression of the hostile star deity
relations.note: Takemikazuchi’s mission is linked to the star’s suppression, but no personal duel is securely narrated.

relations.myth: Suppression of the hostile star deity
relations.note: Takehazuchi receives the decisive star-subduing role within an account connected to Takemikazuchi’s mission.
Takemikazuchi and Ame-no-Koyane are co-enshrined and jointly addressed in Kasuga ritual.
Takemikazuchi and Himegami are co-enshrined and jointly addressed at Kasuga.
The Katori deity Iwainushi is addressed beside Takemikazuchi in the Kasuga festival prayer.
Kasuga systems identify Fukūkenjaku Kannon as Takemikazuchi’s Buddhist original ground.
Some Kasuga interpretations identify Śākyamuni as Takemikazuchi’s Buddhist original ground.
Takemikazuchi becomes both an individual member and an aspect of the collective Kasuga deity.
Takemikazuchi restrains the earthquake-causing catfish with the keystone and sometimes punishes or negotiates with it.
Some earthquake prints make Ebisu substitute for absent Takemikazuchi as guardian of the keystone.
